title: Kembalikan Hutan Mentawai pada Masyarakat Adat
content:
- Masyarakat adat di Kepulauan Mentawai, seperti Suku Umu Samalelet di Pulau Siberut hidup bergantung hutan. Hutan sebagai sumber hidup, dari pangan sampai obat-obatan dan ritual. Menyadari betapa penting ladang dan hutan itu, mereka pun mengusulkan lahan 323 hektar itu jadi hutan adat.
- Suku Samalelet di Desa Rogdok yang mengusulkan hutan adat, juga Suku Saguruwjuw. Selester Saguruwjuw, pemimpin Uma Saguruwjuw, mengatakan, mengusulkan lahan seluas 434 hektar milik komunitas untuk jadi hutan adat, sebagai perubahan cara perjuangan mempertahankan hutan adat.
- Saat ini, Yayasan Citra Mandiri Mentawai (YCMM) dan Aliansi Masyarakat Adat Nusantara (AMAN) Mentawai sedang mendampingi sedikitnya 30 uma dalam proses pengakuan masyarakat adat di Kepulauan Mentawai. Dari 30 uma itu, sembilan sudah memperoleh surat keputusan pengakuan masyarakat adat juga usulan dapat penetapan hutan adat.
- Rifai Lubis, Ketua YCMM meminta, pemerintah menetapkan bekas areal konsesi sebagai kawasan prioritas pemulihan ekologi dan hak masyarakat adat. Pemulihan melalui restorasi hutan, rehabilitasi daerah tangkapan air, percepatan pengakuan masyarakat adat, dan penetapan hutan adat.
Pagi itu, Walter Samalelet beranjak masuk hutan di Pulau Siberut, Kepulauan Mentawai, Sumatera Barat. Kabit di pinggang, ikat kepala luat dengan tiga mawar merah menyala. Kalung manik tudak.
Walter adalah seorang sikerei atau tabib tradisional, yang memberikan pengobatan dengan tumbuhan obat dan ritual.
Lelaki 65 tahun ini gesit melangkah menapaki ladang dengan tanaman campuran. Ia terbentang dari depan rumah hingga berbatasan dengan hutan di kaki bukit di Desa Madobag, Kecamatan Siberut Selatan itu. Ladang dan hutan itu seluas sekitar 323 hektar.
Di ladang tak jauh dari rumahnya ada kolam dangkal dengan banyak tumbuhan keladi. Umbinya sehari-hari mereka andalkan sebagai bahan makanan pokok selain sagu. Di sekitar kolam tanaman pinang mengelilingi.
Semakin menjauhi rumah, aneka pohon buah-buahan seperti rambutan, jengkol, dan durian. Ada juga pohon gaharu dan baiko.
Pohon baiko penting bagi seorang sikerei, karena kulit untuk bahan pembuat kabit, semacam kain yang dililitkan menyerupai celana pendek untuk sikerei.
Di bawah rindang pepohonan rimbun itu aneka jenis tumbuhan obat yang biasa Walter gunakan untuk mengobati warga yang datang berobat. Sebagai seorang sikerei, Walter ahli meramu tumbuhan itu untuk mengobati bermacam penyakit.
“Ini lemu-lemu, daunnya untuk campuran obat sakit perut dan akarnya untuk obat cacing,” katanya.
Dia petik pula tumbuhan keluarga jahe-jahean dengan bunga merah.
“Ini bakgli-bakgli, bunganya digiling dan oleskan ke kepala untuk obat sakit kepala,” katanya.
Sikerei Siberut, kaya dengan pengetahuan tumbuhan obat. Mereka memiliki ratusan jenis tumbuhan obat.
Walter menceritakan sebagian besar tumbuhan obat itu terdapat di dalam hutan di belakang kebunnya.
Pohon juga penanda
Walter mendekati pohon durian besar. Menebas semak di bawahnya. Batang durian sudah penuh lumut. Dia mengikis satu sisinya. Ketika lumut terjatuh, muncul dari kulit pohon itu garis samar penanda setinggi tubuhnya.
Dia mengikis lumut pada bagian lain, tetapi tidak menemukan tanda apa-apa. Garis itu adalah tinggi tubuh ayahnya ketika meninggal.
Walter berusaha mengikis bagian lain, tetapi tidak menemukan goresan gambar kedua telapak tangan dan kedua telapak kaki ayahnya yang sudah meninggal lebih 50 tahun silam.
Pohon durian itu adalah “kirekat” ayah Walter. Di Siberut, lazim seorang yang meninggal mereka buatkan kirekat atau tanda berupa garis tinggi serta gambar telapak tangan dan telapak kaki di batang pohon durian terpilih.
Karena sudah lama, tanda itu tertutup kulit kayu yang terus tumbuh.
“Ini kirekat yang sangat penting untuk mengenang orang tua kami. Ini tidak boleh ditebang, kalau ada orang yang menebangnya akan kena denda yang sangat besar,” kata Walter.
Dia dan komunitasnya menyadari betapa penting ladang dan hutan itu. Itulah alasan Suku Umu Samalelet mengusulkan lahan 323 hektar itu jadi hutan adat.
Dengan bantuan pendampingan Yayasan Citra Mandiri Mentawai (YCMM), mereka sudah pemetaan partisipatif dan mengusulkan hutan adat Uma Samalelet kepada Kementerian Kehutanan. Kini, usulan itu menunggu proses.
“Kami ingin tanah dan hutan kami ada petanya, bisa kami jaga dan kami lindungi. Tidak boleh ada yang mengambil kayunya sembarangan atau berburu, karena hutan ini sangat penting bagi kami, terutama bagi seorang sikerei,” katanya.
“Tanpa hutan, sikerei tidak akan ada.”
Hutan Adat Suku Sagurujuw
Tak hanya Suku Samalelet di Desa Rogdok yang mengusulkan hutan adat, juga Suku Saguruwjuw.
Selester Saguruwjuw, pemimpin Uma Saguruwjuw, mengatakan, mengusulkan lahan seluas 434 hektar milik komunitas untuk jadi hutan adat, sebagai perubahan cara perjuangan mempertahankan hutan adat.
“Dulu, kalau ada perusahaan masuk ke Siberut, ke tanah suku kita, kita akan menolak dengan (melakukan) demonstrasi, sekarang caranya beda, harus kita ikuti,” ujarnya.
Selester juga menekankan hutan sangat penting bagi orang Mentawai. Hutan tempat mengambil berbagai jenis rotan untuk membuat keranjang dan tali temali.
Beberapa jenis bambu juga untuk tempat memasak sagu dan keladi. Juga persediaan pohon untuk material membuat rumah dan keperluan lain.
“Hutan juga tempat mengambil kayu dan tanaman obat. Kalau hutan rusak, kehidupan masyarakat Mentawai akan hancur,” kata Selester.
Berusia sekitar 60 tahun, Selester adalah tokoh masyarakat di Siberut dengan lebih 25 tahun gigih memperjuangkan hutan Siberut dari eksploitasi perusahaan kayu.
Dia masih ingat kejadian 25 tahun silam, pada 24 Mei 2001, ketika jadi Kepala Desa Madobag. Bersama warga desa, dia menolak masuk alat berat perusahaan hak pengusahaan hutan (HPH), yang akan menggarap konsesi seluas 49.650 hektar di Siberut Tengah dan Siberut Utara.
“Kerabat kami di Saibi, Siberut Tengah saat itu meminta bantuan kami menolak alat berat perusahaan yang akan masuk. Kami ikut untuk mempertahankan hutan kami,” katanya mengenang.
Salester menceritakan ketika itu 18 warga Sarereiket di Rogdok dan Ugai pergi naik sampan ke Saibi. Mereka gotong royong membeli bahan bakar minyak untuk perahu motor. Juga menyediakan bersama semua perlengkapan dan konsumsi.
Salah satu alasan kekompakan karena sebagian hutan warga Rereiket juga terkena HPH ini.
Sebelum berangkat, Teu Taloi, rimata atau kepala suku di Ugai, adakan punen (pesta) mukuinu untuk keselamatan rombongan ke Saibi.
Mereka dapat ramuan kunyit untuk oles ke kulit hingga wajah kekuningan. Begitu juga tangan dan kaki.
“Ramuan itu untuk memberi semangat, karena saat itu kami sudah siap berperang, sampan sudah penuh panah,” kata Selester.
Tiba di Muara Siberut, rombongan bergabung dengan warga dari Mailepet dan Tiop. Mereka naik dua boat ke Saibi mengarungi laut selama tiga jam.
“Di Saibi, ternyata kapal ponton yang membawa alat berat ke Subelen sudah datang duluan dua hari sebelumnya. Mereka sudah berhasil diusir warga Saibi dengan membakar basecamp pekerja perusahaan. Akhirnya, kami menginap di rumah warga Saibi, besoknya pulang ke Madobag.”
Beberapa waktu kemudian Koperasi Andalas Madani (KAM) milik Universitas Andalas tetap beroperasi menebang hutan Siberut. Pada 2007, koperasi itu mengembalikan konsesi kepada Menteri Kehutanan dengan alasan merugi.
“Saya harap jangan ada lagi perusahaan kayu masuk ke Siberut dan pulau lain di Mentawai. Saya mengingat nasib generasi mendatang. Hutan mulai habis, satwa mulai habis, hutan Mentawai harus kita selamatkan sekarang. Kalau tidak bisa terlambat, semua akan punah.”
Melawan di era Orba
Rinto Wardana Samaloisa, Bupati Mentawai juga punya kenangan hampir sama dalam menghadapi perusahaan kayu di masa Orde Baru. Dia ingat betul bagaimana bapaknya bercerita tentang konsesi PT Minas Pagai Lumber ( MPL) di Pagai Selatan sebelum beroperasi 1972 di ladang mereka. Konsesi masuk, mereka tak bisa olah ladang.
Warga berupaya protes. Dia ingat, ayahnya lakukan penolakan, sekitar 1994. “Pintu mobil perusahaan yang mengangkut satu pleton polisi itu dikampak sama bapak saya. Jadi bapak saya sempat dibawa ke Polsek Sikakap, Cuma karena masih ada kawan-kawan lamanya di sana, dia bebas lagi.”
Kala itu Orde Baru, kalau melawan bisa nyawa taruhannya. “Dulu, itu kalau berani menghadang kebijakan Orde Baru, bukan badan yang pulang, nama yang pulang.”
Pasca cabut izin
Mentawai alami eksploitasi dari masa ke masa sejak 1971, tak luput Siberut, sebagai pulai terbesar di kabupaten kepulauan itu. Ratusan ribu hektar hutan dalam kuasa perizinan.
Setelah beroperasi lebih 20 tahun, eksploitasi setop pada 1993 terkait program konservasi di Siberut dengan kucuran pinjaman Asian Development Bank (ADB) US$24,5 juta. Program enam tahun itu mensyaratkan penghentian eksploitasi hutan.
Sebagian bagian program, pada 1993 itu Pulau Siberut bagian barat seluas 190.500 hektar jadi Taman Nasional Siberut. Program itu masuk dalam proyek konservasi keanekaragaman hayati untuk Taman Nasional Siberut.
Penghentian penebangan hutan di Siberut tidak berlangsung lama. Setelah program konservasi berakhir pada 1999, Menteri Kehutanan kembali mengeluarkan dua izin HPH baru di Siberut.
Pertama, Land Grant Colage (LGC) kepada Universitas Andalas seluas 49.650 hektar. Pada 2001, berubah nama menjadi hak pengelolaan hutan alam Universitas Andalas melalui Koperasi Andalas Madani (koperasi khusus), dengan operator lapangan PT Sinar Minang Sejahtera (SMS).
Kedua, pada 2004 berupa HPH seluas 49.440 hektar kepada PT Salaki Summa Sejahtera (SSS).
Operasional KAM bangkrut dan berhenti pada 2007. Di kawasan hutan itu, Siti Nurbaya, Menteri Lingkungan Hidup dan Kehutanan keluarkan izin HTI untuk PT Biomass Andalan Energi (BAE) 19.876 hektar Desember 2018.
Setelah SSS beroperasi lebih 20 tahun, pemerintah cabut izin itu pada 20 Januari 2026 pasca bencana banjir bandang dahsyat melanda Sumatra. Sedang BAE, belum beroperasi sejak 2018 juga masuk daftar pencabutan.
Pemerintah juga cabut izin HPH di Pagai, MPL, sejak 1976 beroperasi dengan konsensi 78.000 hektar di Pulau Pagai Utara dan Pagai Selatan.
Rifai Lubis, Ketua YCMM meminta, pemerintah menetapkan bekas areal konsesi sebagai kawasan prioritas pemulihan ekologi dan hak masyarakat adat.
Pemulihan melalui restorasi hutan, rehabilitasi daerah tangkapan air, percepatan pengakuan masyarakat adat, dan penetapan hutan adat.
“Kami juga mendesak pemerintah mempercepat penetapan hutan adat bagi uma yang telah memperoleh pengakuan serta menyelesaikan verifikasi terhadap calon hutan adat lainnya,” katanya.
Saat ini, YCMM dan Aliansi Masyarakat Adat Nusantara (AMAN) Mentawai sedang mendampingi sedikitnya 30 uma dalam proses pengakuan masyarakat adat di Kepulauan Mentawai.
Dari 30 uma itu, sembilan sudah memperoleh surat keputusan pengakuan masyarakat adat juga usulan dapat penetapan hutan adat.
Adapun antara lain usulan hutan adat itu, Uma Sibagau (8.683 hektar), Uma Saponduruk (1.874), Uma Samongilailai (1.400), Uma Sakerebau Mailepet (1.342), Uma Sirirui (1.198), dan Uma Saerejen (1.150 hektar).
Rifai bilang, sebagian wilayah yang mereka usulkan sebagai hutan adat masih tumpang tindih dengan kawasan konservasi maupun izin pemanfaatan hutan.
“Kami meminta pemerintah segera menyelesaikan proses verifikasi dan penetapan hutan adat, terutama bagi uma yang telah memperoleh pengakuan sebagai masyarakat adat.”
Rinto mengatakan, pencabutan izin itu seharusnya jadi pintu masuk masyarakat mendapat kembali hak pengelolaan hutan mereka.
“Pilihan yang saya inginkan adalah perhutanan sosial. Masyarakat harus memperoleh kesempatan mengelola lahannya sendiri dengan pendampingan dan kontrol pemerintah.”
Bagi Rinto, keterlibatan pemerintah tetap perlu untuk memastikan pengelolaan hutan tidak menyimpang dari ketentuan. Pemerintah, katanya, dapat melakukan pembinaan atau pun menjatuhkan sanksi apabila menemukan pelanggaran.
Skema semacam itu, katanya, memberikan ruang lebih besar bagi masyarakat daripada pengelolaan perusahaan yang memiliki modal, jaringan dan dukungan hukum jauh lebih kuat.
“Perusahaan tidak hanya mengambil kayu, juga memecah hubungan sosial.”
Meski begitu, katanya, pencabutan izin belum sepenuhnya menjawab persoalan penguasaan hutan di Mentawai. Rinto khawatir kawasan yang perusahaan swasta bukan kembali kepada masyarakat hukum adat, melainkan beralih kepada badan usaha milik negara.
Kekhawatiran itu muncul setelah dia mengikuti rapat dengan pemerintah pusat. Dalam pertemuan itu, dia memperoleh penjelasan bahwa kawasan kehutanan bekas konsesi dapat diserahkan kepada Perum Perhutani melalui anak usahanya, Inhutani. Sedangkan, kawasan perkebunan sawit oleh Agrinas.
“Kalau demikian, yang terjadi hanya pergantian pengelola dari perusahaan swasta kepada perusahaan negara,” katanya.
Menurut Rinto, penyerahan kawasan bekas konsesi kepada masyarakat tidak dapat dilakukan tanpa dukungan memadai.
Masyarakat, katanya, tak memiliki modal, peralatan, maupun jaringan pemasaran setara dengan perusahaan untuk mengelola kawasan dalam bentang sangat luas.
Karena itu, dia gusulkan kawasan bekas konsesi bagi ke dalam unit pengelolaan dengan luasan yang realistis bagi kelompok masyarakat.
Penyerahan itu, katanya, harus dengan kepastian hak, pendampingan teknis, pembiayaan, dan akses terhadap pasar.
Cara masyarakat memanfaatkan hutan, katanya, tidak sama dengan pola kerja korporasi yang berorientasi pada produksi berskala besar.
“Masyarakat mengambil seperlunya dan memelihara sebanyak mungkin. Mereka membutuhkan kepastian hak dan dukungan agar dapat mengelola kawasan itu dengan baik.”

title: « Toutes les charges sont comprises, il y a un espace de travail, une salle de détente, une laverie… » : quand les résidences étudiantes privées font le plein
content:
Cassandra a eu beau s’y prendre en février pour une rentrée en septembre, elle n’a pas eu l’embarras du choix. « J’ai commencé à chercher bien avant de savoir si j’étais acceptée par l’école, et il restait déjà très peu de logements disponibles », souligne l’étudiante en 2e année à l’institut de formation en soins infirmiers de Rouen (comme d’autres personnes interrogées, elle n’a pas souhaité donner son nom). Avec ses parents, et après cinq visites de studios en location dans le parc privé traditionnel, son choix s’est porté sur une résidence étudiante privée.
« Toutes les charges sont comprises, c’est sécurisé, il y a un espace de travail, une salle de détente, une laverie… », liste Cassandra, 19 ans. Son forfait comprend la location d’un studio de 26 mètres carrés ; la consommation d’eau chaude, d’électricité et de gaz ; l’accès aux espaces communs ; la fourniture du Wi-Fi et, cerise sur le gâteau, un service de ménage toutes les six semaines. La résidence se trouve à cinq minutes à pied de son école et du centre hospitalier universitaire. « Il y a deux sas pour accéder à la résidence et, sur place, deux étudiants qui sont référents en cas de problème. Ça a beaucoup rassuré mes parents », ajoute-t-elle.

title: 33,600 more get jobs, but SA’s unemployment crisis deepens
content:
Story audio is generated using AI
The department of employment and labour says it placed 33,600 job seekers in employment and other opportunities during the first quarter of the 2026/27 financial year, as South Africa grapples with an unemployment rate of 33.6%.
The figures were disclosed in a parliamentary response after MK Party MP Siyabonga Percival Mkhize questioned employment and labour minister Nomakhosazana Meth on what interventions her department had implemented to create permanent and sustainable employment rather than temporary work opportunities.
Mkhize also asked how many permanent jobs had resulted from each intervention, how much had been spent and what measurable targets the department had set to reduce unemployment by the end of the financial year.
Meth said more than 456,000 unemployed job seekers were registered on the department’s Employment Services of South Africa (Essa) system during the first quarter.
“In the 2026/27 financial year, quarter one, the department provided various services to the unemployed work seekers. Work seekers that were enrolled on the department’s Essa system totalled 456,094, counselling services that were provided totalled 144,104, and the number of work seekers placed, for quarter one of 2026, equalled to 33,600,” she said.
Meth said the 33,600 placements included formal jobs, apprenticeships, project opportunities and training opportunities.
Limpopo had the highest number of placements at 8,688, followed by Gauteng with 7,238.
The Eastern Cape recorded 3,797 placements, KwaZulu-Natal 3,290, Free State 2,639, Western Cape 2,554 and Mpumalanga 2,174.
The Northern Cape recorded 1,613 placements while North West had the lowest number at 1,607.
The figures come as the country’s unemployment rate climbed to its highest level in four years. Stats SA’s Quarterly Labour Force Survey for the second quarter of 2026 showed the official unemployment rate increased from 32.7% in the first quarter to 33.6%.
The number of unemployed people increased by 345,000 to 8.5-million, while the number of employed people decreased by 16,000 to 16.7-million.
Young people continue to bear a disproportionate share of the unemployment crisis. The number of unemployed people aged between 15 and 34 years old increased by 264,000 to 5-million between the first and second quarters.
The youth unemployment rate increased by 1.5 percentage points to 47.4%, while the number of employed young people declined by 40,000 to 5.6-million.
On the cost of its employment interventions, Meth said public employment services were offered free of charge and funded through the department’s overall budget, meaning there was no specific amount allocated to each service.
“For the 2026/27 financial year, given the budget allocated, the department will target placing 75,000 work seekers into employment opportunities, and a further 130,000 job opportunities will be targeted through its partnership with the National Pathway Management Network. The department aims to create 1-million work opportunities as part of its MTDP target, plus a further 1-million by its entities,” said Meth.
The department’s first-quarter figure of 33,600 represents about 45% of its annual target of placing 75,000 work seekers into employment opportunities.
The department’s response did not provide a breakdown of how many of the 33,600 placements were permanent jobs, as opposed to apprenticeships, project or training opportunities.

title: Nigeria records W’Africa’s first telerobotic surgery across 500km
content:
As part of efforts to expand access to technology-driven advanced surgeries, the Redeemer’s Health Village has performed what it described as the first telerobotic surgery in West Africa.
The procedure was carried out at the Redeemer’s Health Village in Mowe, Ogun State, during the weekend.
Tele-robotic surgery, also known as remote surgery, allows a surgeon to operate on a patient from another location.
The procedure, a right radical nephrectomy, was carried out by RHV in collaboration with RoboMed Global and Nisa Premier Hospital, Abuja, and involved surgeons at RHV remotely operating on a patient at the Abuja-based hospital.
Speaking after the surgery, the Chief Executive Officer of RHV, Dr. Adedamola Dada, said the successful telerobotic procedure and other robot-assisted surgeries performed by RHV signal a new dawn in Nigeria.
“It’s a huge breakthrough, and then of course, it is the first time telesurgery is done in West Africa,” he said.
Dada said the surgical robot at Abuja hospital was connected to the robotic control system at RHV through an internet connection.
“What this simply means is that for very complicated cases where we don’t even have the manpower in the country, surgeons can stay in the United States and operate on that patient here,” he said.
Before the telerobotic surgery, the RHV boss said the facility had, on the same day, carried out robotic-assisted pyeloplasty surgery on a 28-year-old patient.
“What we have done is called a pyeloplasty. It’s an attempt to reconstruct the pelvis, remove the obstructions, and ensure that the urine flows freely. And for those of us who were in the theatre, it was pretty obvious immediately that the obstruction was removed; the urine started flowing very freely. So it’s a new day in our country,” he said.
He, however, urged the Federal Government to support the training of medical professionals in robotic surgery, saying developing local manpower is essential to sustaining the country’s growing adoption of the technology.
Dada said government support through sponsorship and scholarships would enable more surgeons, nurses, biomedical engineers and other specialists to acquire the skills required to perform and support robotic procedures in Nigeria.
He said, “Most of the time, the equipment is really not a challenge; the challenge now is the manpower. We have a lot of private sector people, organisations who would be able to bridge that gap in terms of procuring the robots.”
Dada added, “The government needs to support and sponsor Nigerians- the surgeons, nurses, biomedical engineers – who would want to come for the training by awarding them scholarships so that in another one or two or three years, we would have a lot of professionals who can do this.”
Also speaking, the robotic surgeon who led the procedure, Prof. Obi Davies-Ekwenna, said the feat could help Nigeria bridge geographical barriers to expand access to complex procedures across the country.
Davies-Ekwenna said the remote surgery was a pointer to the game-changing nature of technology in delivering precision healthcare in Nigeria.
“We were able to operate on a patient in Abuja, 500 kilometres away. We were able to operate on a patient with a kidney tumour, a cancer tumour. And so that was successful.
“It means access to experts from within and outside the country. Telesurgery can be done from any part of the world with precision, with excellent results,” the robotic surgeon said.
On his part, the RHV Board Chairman, Dr Kunle Onokoya, said that with robotic surgery, many procedures considered inoperable are now being done successfully.
“The kind of surgery that otherwise would have been inoperable, meaning that the risk from surgery was too great, is now being done with robot-assisted surgery,” he said.

title: 'We're one people' - a young Tongan man's te reo Māori journey
content:
Over the years, 21-year-old Siaosi (George) Lavelua (Kolomotu'a, Makave) has often made the trip north to the Waitangi Treaty Grounds with freshly made 'otai in tow.
His whānau business, Lav's 'otai - dealing in the much loved Polynesian drink that typically mixes coconut and fruit - is the longest-serving 'otai operation in Tāmaki Makaurau.
It has become a familiar fixture at Waitangi celebrations, Auckland night markets and various community events across the region.
"It's something I've grown up around my whole life. Wherever there's a big event, we're usually there serving 'otai and meeting people," Lavelua said.
Over the years, events such as Waitangi have become extra special for Lavelua - a Tongan who has dedicated over five years of his life learning te reo Māori.
"When I was able to go up there (Waitangi) and then converse with a bunch of different people in te reo Māori, just seeing the connections and friends and people that you can make just through speaking te reo, it definitely, yeah, made me very appreciative to be able to learn the language," Lavelua said.
Lavelua grew up in central Auckland, speaking Tongan at home with his parents.
His reo journey began as a year 9 at Auckland Grammar School, and was initially an opportunity for him to spend class time with other tauira Māori and Pasifika.
"For the first three years of my schooling, in every other class except Te reo Māori, I was the only, like one or two Pacific or Māori people in my classes," Lavelua said.
"I just wanted to be with other people from the Pacific, and so then I took te reo Māori."
Lavelua loved it so much that he stuck it out until year 13, and quickly realised the merging similarities between the Tongan language and the Māori language.
"As I started to learn the language, I noticed that there were so many similarities in terms of, like, old Tongan," he said.
"There was quite a lot of words or the same sentence structure that mirrored exactly what I was learning, what I speak at home. And so it just made my journey a whole lot easier."
While it wasn't an 'easy journey, Lavelua said it was well-worth the investment.
Crossover
Online, he has began sharing content speaking te reo Māori.
People often comment on how impressive his trilingualism is, something Lavelua said reinforced his own appreciation for the Tongan language.
"Since I grew up speaking Tongan, it was always sort of something on like a back burner, it wasn't necessarily something that I thought too much about," Lavelua said.
That changed as he watched how people responded to his reo, including Māori who frequently tell him of their desire to learn and speak their own language one day.
"It's really a deeper love for my own language and my own culture. And just seeing how blessed I was to retain that."
"Growing up, I've always had such a deep respect for the Māori culture and Māori people," he said.
"I think it's a beautiful thing what Māori had done here in New Zealand, and Aotearoa, being able to retain the culture and traditions and languages, even all the way up to religion, and that's something that we certainly didn't really have in other parts of the Pacific, being very Christianised and things."
The values between cultures cross over, too, Lavelua said.
When asked which te ao Māori principles resonate, he landed on whanaungatanga.
"Hospitality and that sort of relationship they have with other people…it's about the home, it's the relationships of those around us, the community, the environment," he said.
And Lavelua said that point is one of the real lessons he came to learn while learning te reo Māori.
"There are some people who very distinctly categorise Māori and Pasifika as two separate categories, or two separate people," he said.
"But then definitely through learning te reo and learning a lot more about the culture, you really see that overlap and like that true understanding that you actually are one people at the end of the day."
One of the biggest surprises on his journey so far has been understanding the historical relationships between Pacific and Māori.
Lavelua began reading Pacific history, and came across accounts of Pacific sovereigns - he points to King Tāwhiao, alongside Tongan and Hawaiian royalty - who would write to one another as colonisation took hold.
"They all had actually been writing letters between each other to sort of help each other maintain their own sovereignty," he said.
" Seeing that back in the day, specifically with these leaders that we had in our communities, it was definitely heartwarming to see and really opened my mind on just how interconnected the Pacific really is, and how interconnected the Pacific should be."
Journey
Now based in Brisbane, working across marketing and hospitality, Lavelua said distance from Aotearoa has sharpened the meaning of events such as Te Wiki o Te Reo Māori, and what they mean to him.
It's a good reminder, he said, to celebrate the week, identity, and community.
He also has advice for other Pasifika and non-Māori who are thinking of undertaking their reo journey.
"Just give it a crack, just give it a go. I don't think that anybody can ever be perfect in a language. I definitely wasn't perfect when learning te reo Māori, I'm still not perfect at this point, but that's definitely something that holds a lot of people back.
His favourite whakataukī encompasses this message well.
"Tūwhitia te hopo, mairangatia te angitū! Feel the fear and do it anyway. I think that's fitting when it comes to learning languages, or anywhere in life."

title: Construction exoskeletons may help workers spot hazards by reducing fatigue
content:
Taking some of the physical strain off construction workers could do more than reduce fatigue. New research from Texas A&M University suggests it may also help them recognize hazards around them.
In a field study of 16 construction workers, researchers found that workers using a passive lower-back exoskeleton experienced 37% less fatigue and improved their hazard recognition performance by 29%. The findings point to a connection between reducing physical fatigue and helping workers remain attentive to potential dangers on the job site.
"Construction safety involves both your body and your mind," said lead author Prosper Gbiengu, a graduate research assistant and doctoral student in the Department of Construction Science. "If you reduce fatigue, that helps keep the worker more attentive, and you're able to identify more hazards."
The study, published in ASCE Open: Multidisciplinary Journal of Civil Engineering, adds a new dimension to research on wearable exoskeletons, which has largely focused on their ability to reduce strain.
Testing exoskeletons in the field
Exoskeletons can support different parts of the body, including the arms, back and knees. The model used in the field study was a prototype passive lower-back exoskeleton designed to reduce the effort required during physically demanding work.
Chukwuma Nnaji, associate professor in the Department of Construction Science, said exoskeletons remain relatively uncommon on construction sites but are more commonly used in structured workplaces such as automobile manufacturing, logistics and warehousing, where workers are more likely to repeat the same movements. Construction presents a more complicated challenge.
"You will rarely find a company that is fully deploying exoskeletons," Nnaji said. "In construction, we tend to be more dynamic—moving from one subtask to another to complete one larger task, so the movements tend to be different."
To examine how the technology performs under those conditions, construction workers completed 3-hour sessions performing their normal work both with and without an exoskeleton. Researchers measured their fatigue and showed them images of construction hazards before and after each session, asking them to identify the hazards and assess the associated risks.
In addition to workers being less fatigued and better at recognizing hazards while using the exoskeleton, the researchers also found that workers who experienced smaller increases in fatigue tended to show greater improvements in hazard recognition. This suggests a connection between workers' physical state and their safety-related cognitive performance.
Nnaji said the findings add another layer to the evidence that exoskeletons can reduce workers' physical exertion: If workers are less fatigued, they may have more cognitive resources available to focus on what is happening around them.
"If you're able to focus on the task because you're less fatigued, then you're better able to detect things that might be anomalies in your environment," he said.
That can be particularly important in construction, where workers must continually recognize and respond to changing conditions around them.
"For us in construction, that is foundational because our environment is extremely dynamic," Nnaji said. "It's changing often, and you need to be aware of what's going on around you."
Managing fatigue on the job site
For construction companies, the findings suggest that managing physical fatigue may have implications beyond reducing strain on workers' bodies. Nnaji cautioned, however, against viewing exoskeletons as a universal solution. "Exoskeletons are not a silver bullet," he said.
Instead, Nnaji said companies should first look for opportunities to eliminate or reduce risks through the way work is designed. When physical demands cannot be eliminated, technologies such as exoskeletons may provide another way to reduce the amount of exertion required from workers.
The research team is continuing to test exoskeletons on job sites and work with industry partners to better understand how the devices can be designed and used safely for construction work. Nnaji said collaboration with workers is critical to developing technology that addresses the realities of construction rather than problems defined solely in a laboratory.
"If you design solutions in a vacuum, you will not be able to solve the real problem," Nnaji said. "You need to engage with people. You need to be on the job site. You need to see how jobs are being executed."

title: Gattino affetto da una grave condizione neurologica torna a camminare grazie a una sedia a rotelle fatta di Lego
content:
Gattino affetto da una grave condizione neurologica torna a camminare grazie a una sedia a rotelle fatta di Lego
A soli 4 mesi di età, il piccolo gattino Rex non aveva mai mosso un passo autonomamente a causa di una grave condizione neurologica nota come ipoplasia cerebellare, comunemente chiamata sindrome del gatto traballante. Questa patologia compromette lo sviluppo del cervelletto, alterando irrimediabilmente l’equilibrio e la coordinazione dei movimenti. Quando è stato accolto dai volontari del gruppo di soccorso Rescue Connect e affidato alle cure della soccorritrice Jennifer Witkowski, le sue possibilità di ripresa sembravano estremamente ridotte. Il micio appariva poco reattivo, ma grazie alle cure quotidiane ha iniziato lentamente a mostrare segnali di miglioramento e un timido desiderio di muoversi.
Tuttavia, le normali sedie a rotelle in commercio per animali presentavano due problemi insormontabili: un costo proibitivo stimato intorno ai 1.800 dollari e l’inadeguatezza per un cucciolo in rapida crescita, che avrebbe reso il supporto inutilizzabile dopo appena un mese e mezzo. Di fronte a questa spesa proibitiva, i volontari hanno cercato un’alternativa economica e modulabile, ispirandosi a un’idea già vista in un altro rifugio e rivolgendosi al negozio specializzato Bricks & Minifigs a Wilmington, nella Carolina del Nord.
La geniale invenzione di Michael Hawley e i primi passi verso la normalità
All’interno del negozio specializzato, l’impiegato Michael Hawley ha accettato con entusiasmo la sfida di progettare una carrozzina su misura. Forte di un’infanzia trascorsa a costruire con i leggendari mattoncini e memore della sua precedente esperienza con un cane affetto dalla stessa sindrome, Mr. Wiggles, Hawley ha assemblato un supporto perfettamente calibrato sulle esigenze del felino. Dopo alcuni aggiustamenti tecnici, la sedia a rotelle in Lego è stata testata con risultati sbalorditivi.
Appena sistemato nel dispositivo, il micio ha iniziato a camminare quasi immediatamente, ritrovando la capacità di spostarsi e proseguire la riabilitazione. Anche se la carrozzina non può cancellare la malattia neurologica, gli ha regalato uno strumento fondamentale per vivere una vita dignitosa e anche una casa dato che è stato preso in affido da una nuova famiglia.

title: »Zgodila se mi je nesreča. Naj moja zgodba ne postane vaša« (video)
content:
Oglejte si, kako deluje novi sistem COPS v Račah in zakaj je pomemben za varnejšo šolsko pot:
Janez Hudej je svojo zgodbo delil tudi z učenci Osnovne šole Rače, kjer so ob odprtju novega prometnega sistema govorili o varnejših šolskih poteh. Zavarovalnica Triglav, Občina Rače - Fram in podjetje Tenzor so ob prehodu na Mariborski cesti v bližini osnovne šole namreč postavili nov inteligentni prometni sistem COPS@zebra LITE (Collision Preventing Safety System), ki voznike opozarja na prehod za pešce in tako prispeva k večji prometni varnosti v šolskem okolišu.
Hudej je učencem pokazal fotografijo, posneto dan pred nesrečo, ko je kot mlad fant po poklicni šoli že hodil v službo, doma pomagal na manjši kmetiji, rad plesal in se ukvarjal s športom. S prijatelji se je dogovoril za nedeljsko vožnjo z motorji, pred potjo domov pa je spil tudi nekaj alkohola. Ko so se proti večeru odpravljali, luč na njegovem motorju ni delovala, popraviti je niso mogli. »Saj ni problema, če luč ne gori, jaz bom peljal naprej,« se spominja svoje odločitve. Prijatelja naj bi mu z drugim motorjem svetila od zadaj. Nato je pospešil in se jima oddaljil. Kaj se je zgodilo zatem, je izvedel iz policijskega zapisnika: zapeljal je s ceste, zadel podrto drevo in nezavesten obležal. Našli so ga šele naslednje jutro.
Zaradi posledic poškodbe hrbtenjače bo vse življenje uporabljal invalidski voziček. V bolnišnici je preživel štiri mesece, nato je odšel na rehabilitacijo v Ljubljano. Po vrnitvi domov se je moral na življenje z vozičkom šele navaditi. Učence, ki so takoj prepoznali njegove nevarne odločitve, je opozoril, naj sami izberejo varnejšo pot.
Učenci vedo, kje vozniki vozijo prehitro
V Zavodu VOZIM zato mlade vključujejo v raziskovanje lastnega prometnega okolja. Na srečanju so učenci predstavili nekaj svojih predlogov za boljšo prometno varnost v okolici osnovne šole, ki so jih na podlagi konkretnih podatkov pripravili na delavnicah skupaj z Zavodom VOZIM. »Opazili smo, da okoli šole vozniki vozijo zelo hitro,« je preprosto in neposredno povedala ena od učenk. »Do šole naj naredijo kolesarsko pot in uredijo avtobusno postajo,« sta predlagala učenca. Otroci promet na šolski poti spremljajo vsak dan: čakajo ob cesti, hodijo do avtobusnega postajališča in opazujejo avtomobile, zato so dobri poznavalci lokalnih prometnih razmer.
Opozarjali so tudi na ravnanje udeležencev v prometu, v svojih sporočilih pa vrstnike spomnili, naj spremljajo dogajanje okoli sebe in naj telefon spravijo v žep. Ker so predloge slišali tako otroci kot predstavniki občine, lahko upamo, da bo kakšna od idej v prihodnje tudi resnično zaživela.
»Vaši predlogi lahko nekaj spremenijo v družbi,« je učence za njihovo vlogo aktivnega državljanstva pohvalil David Razboršek, direktor Zavoda VOZIM. Naloga odraslih je, da jih slišijo in izvedljive zamisli prenesejo v prakso. »Tudi sin mi je nekoč potožil, da voznik šolskega avtobusa vozi prehitro, in ko je to končno omenil tudi v šoli, so se očitno pogovorili z voznikom, ki je pripombo upošteval. Tudi to je primer dobrega sodelovanja,« je še dodal.
Ob šoli so izmerili tudi 109 kilometrov na uro
»Novi sistem COPS@zebra LITE ob šoli je od namestitve do odprtja zabeležil najvišjo hitrost 109 kilometrov na uro. Kar 14 % vseh vozil je prekoračilo hitrost,« je povedal Miha Senčar, direktor podjetja Tenzor. Gre za podatek s ceste, ki jo otroci prečkajo na vsakodnevni poti v šolo in domov. Prehod je na območju trikotnega križišča na Mariborski cesti. Zaradi poteka ceste in omejene preglednosti ga je iz ene smeri težje opaziti, zato je pomembno, da voznik prehod zazna dovolj zgodaj in pravočasno zmanjša hitrost. Sistem je postavljen tako, da opozorilno signalizacijo vidijo vozniki iz obeh smeri prihoda v križišče.
Kot je povedala Ana Cergolj Kebler, vodja oddelka za trženjsko komuniciranje v Zavarovalnici Triglav, skrb za šolske poti povezuje z razlogom, zaradi katerega se s prometno varnostjo ukvarjajo tudi starši: želijo vedeti, da bo njihov otrok varno prišel v šolo. »Pravzaprav so otroci gonilo, pogon, vzrok in navdih za izboljševanje prometne varnosti. Varnejšo mobilnost ustvarjajo ukrepi, skupaj s tehnologijo, podatki in preventivo. Prav sistemi COPS so primer takšnega povezovanja – na eni od lokacij je sistem na prehitro vožnjo ob približevanju prehodu opozoril več kot 40 odstotkov voznikov, kar pokaže, kako velik del voznikov potrebuje tovrstne opomnike. Letošnji Evropski teden mobilnosti v ospredje postavlja mobilnost za vse generacije. Novi sistem v Račah je konkreten primer rešitve tam, kjer je varnost še posebej pomembna: na vsakodnevni šolski poti otrok.« Pri izbiri lokacij zato upoštevajo tako prometno obremenjenost kot ljudi, ki te poti uporabljajo.
Znak se odzove na prihod vozila
Kako takšno opozarjanje deluje? Miha Senčar, direktor podjetja Tenzor, pojasnjuje, da je COPS@zebra LITE aktivni prometni znak, ki s pomočjo radarja zazna vozilo, ko se to približuje prehodu. Takrat se vklopi utripanje, ki voznika opozori dovolj zgodaj, da lahko zmanjša hitrost in pozornost usmeri na prehod ter ljudi ob njem.
Sistem hkrati zbira podatke, s katerimi je mogoče spremljati dogajanje na cesti. Beleži gostoto prometa, hitrosti in prekoračitve dovoljene hitrosti. Za presojo njegovega delovanja je pomembno tudi, kaj voznik naredi po opozorilu. Če med približevanjem prehodu zmanjša hitrost, se to pokaže v meritvah. »V naslednjem obdobju bomo spremljali, ali so se vozniki na to utripanje odzvali,« napoveduje Senčar. Preverjali bodo zmanjševanje hitrosti med približevanjem znaku, tako da bodo dobili natančnejšo sliko vožnje na tem delu šolske poti. Za občino so takšni podatki uporabni tudi pri nadaljnjem urejanju prometnih poti.
Osnova za odločanje: dve milijardi skupnih kilometrov
Pri odločanju, kam postaviti sistem COPS, v Zavarovalnici Triglav povežejo podatke in izkušnje lokalnega okolja. Preverijo razpoložljive meritve in se posvetujejo z občino. Pri tem jim pomaga brezplačni DRAJV zemljevid, nekakšen »kolektivni zemljevid naših voženj«, ki nastaja iz podatkov uporabnikov aplikacije DRAJV in omogoča vpogled v prometne izzive na slovenskih cestah. Pri pregledu posameznega odseka jih zanimajo hitrost, zaviranja, nagla pospeševanja in ravnanje v ovinkih.
Podatke o svojih vožnjah vsak mesec prostovoljno prispeva več kot 56.000 voznikov in skupaj so z aplikacijo doslej prevozili več kot dve milijardi kilometrov. To je osnova, ki jo nato dopolnijo s poznavanjem posamezne ceste in potreb ljudi ob njej.
Za Zavarovalnico Triglav je povezovanje podatkov, tehnoloških rešitev in preventive del dolgoletnega dela na področju prometne varnosti. Kot pojasni Ana Cergolj Kebler, so pred dvanajstimi leti slovenska podjetja, ustanove in inovatorje povabili k iskanju novih rešitev in med predlogi so bili tudi sistemi COPS. Sledile so postavitve na nevarnih lokacijah v sodelovanju z občinami in spremljanje, kaj se je po namestitvi spremenilo.
Na analiziranih lokacijah okoli 80 odstotkov manj nesreč
Zavarovalnica Triglav je skupaj z občinami in slovenskimi tehnološkimi podjetji podprla postavitev že več kot 130 sistemov COPS po Sloveniji. Namenjeni so različnim prometnim situacijam, od prehodov za pešce do križišč in drugih nepreglednih mest. Posamezno rešitev je treba izbrati in umestiti glede na nevarnosti na konkretni lokaciji.
V okviru letošnjih aktivnosti Triglava je novi COPS@zebra LITE začel delovati tudi v občini Kidričevo, na prehodu na Tovarniški cesti. Tam se vsak dan pelje približno 4.500 vozil. Cesta vodi proti večjim zaposlitvenim središčem, v bližini sta trgovina in železniška postaja, prehod pa uporabljajo tudi otroci in starejši. Pri takšnih postavitvah je treba razumeti vsakodnevne poti ljudi: kam hodijo po opravkih, kako pridejo do postaje in kje morajo prečkati prometno cesto.
Pri presoji rezultatov po besedah Ane Cergolj Kebler uporabljajo podatke policije in Agencije za varnost prometa. Pogledajo statistiko nesreč za tri leta pred postavitvijo, nato pa dogajanje spremljajo še približno tri leta po njej. Takšna primerjava pokaže, kako se je spremenilo število nesreč na obravnavanem mestu.
Po podatkih ponudnika sistemov COPS so na lokacijah, za katere so opravili analizo pred postavitvijo in po njej, ugotovili povprečno približno 80 odstotkov manj prometnih nesreč. Ob številki ostaja pomembno tudi vprašanje, kako izbrano mesto uporabljajo pešci, kolesarji in vozniki. Manj nesreč pomeni manj ljudi s poškodbami in manj družin, ki se morajo spoprijeti z njihovimi posledicami.
Na koncu je Janez Hudej učencem zaželel, da jim nikoli ne bi bilo treba pripovedovati podobno pretresljive zgodbe, kot je njegova, in dodal še eno ključno misel: »Kar je še bolj pomembno, pa je, da moja zgodba ne bi postala zgodba nekoga tretjega zaradi vas.«
Sami kot vozniki pa lahko k bolj varnim cestam in potem v okolici šol in vrtcev prispevamo tako, da smo zgled drugim in umaknemo nogo s plina.

title: Three-hour ordeal to rescue man trapped in 30-metre rock crevice
content:
Man rescued after falling down 30-metre rock crevice in San Remo, south-east of Melbourne
A man has been rescued after falling down a 30-metre rock crevice at San Remo, about 120 kilometres south-east of Melbourne.
Emergency services were called to the coastal region after reports of a man falling and becoming trapped in a rock crevice off George Bass Coastal Walk about 2:10pm on Saturday.
Emergency crews were able to communicate with the 50-year-old, who told them he had broken his leg, but they struggled to gain access to him due to the difficult terrain and rising tide.
An Ambulance Victoria helicopter was called in, with other personnel from Fire Rescue Victoria, Country Fire Authority, the State Emergency Service (SES), Air Wing, Search and Rescue Squad, Life Saving Victoria and Water Police working together to rescue the man.
Search and Rescue officers finally entered the crevice to assess him, and the man was winched to safety about 5:30pm.
He was flown to Royal Melbourne Hospital in a stable condition with non-life-threatening injuries.

title: 100% job placement guarantee goes unfulfilled: MBA graduate drags institute to court, gets full refund
content:
A Punjab consumer commission has ordered a training company to refund an MBA graduate’s fees. The dispute concerned a course advertised with a promise of “100% guaranteed placement”.
The Gurdaspur district consumer commission passed its order on 16 September. It directed Eduinx Education Services to refund ₹84,960 to Harish Malhotra, The Times of India reported.
The commission also awarded ₹10,000 for mental tension and harassment. Another ₹5,000 was granted towards his legal expenses, according to TOI.
Malhotra joined an online programme covering artificial intelligence (AI) in product management. According to his complaint, an advertisement promising guaranteed placement influenced his decision.
The MBA graduate paid ₹84,960 through a credit card on 12 July 2025. He completed the course and received his certificate on 24 November 2025.
However, Malhotra alleged that the promised job had never materialised despite repeated follow-ups. He said the company had kept extending its timelines. He then approached the commission, seeking a refund and compensation.
Malhotra claimed he had remained unemployed for more than 10 months. He sought ₹6 lakh for financial losses and damage to his career continuity. He also requested ₹30,000 towards legal expenses.
Eduinx denied the allegations and described itself as a training and career-support platform. It argued that employers, rather than the platform, made hiring decisions.
The company said its guarantee covered interview preparation, profile improvement and contact with employers. It also claimed Malhotra participated in recruitment processes involving several companies.
Eduinx alleged that he had rejected opportunities outside his preferred locations, Gurugram and Delhi-NCR.
The commission examined whether these recruitment efforts fulfilled the advertised promise. President Lalit Mohan Dogra and member B S Matharu found that they did not.
The bench distinguished between arranging interviews and actually securing placement. It said any limits on the guarantee should have been clearly disclosed during enrolment.
The commission also rejected unsupported claims linking the outcome to Malhotra’s interview performance. Eduinx did not produce employer assessments or communications establishing rejection on that basis.
WhatsApp messages showed that some vacancies were shared with him. However, the commission found these messages did not establish definite employment offers or successful placement.
“A mere suggestion of a vacancy cannot be equated with an employment offer as promised. Nor can a recruitment lead, screening call or interview be treated as equivalent to a successful placement,” TOI quoted the commission as stating.
“Therefore, even after taking the WhatsApp conversations at their face value, the evidence falls short of establishing that the opposite parties fulfilled the substantive placement representation,” it added.
It held that the unfulfilled commitment amounted to deficient service. The inadequately-qualified placement guarantee also amounted to an unfair trade practice.
However, the commission rejected the ₹6 lakh compensation claim because supporting documents were insufficient.
Payment must follow within 45 days of receiving the order’s copy. Otherwise, the refund attracts 9% annual interest from the deposit until actual repayment.

title: Evaluating functional outcomes following hand therapy in cubital tunnel release.
content: Cubital tunnel syndrome is the second most common nerve compression of the upper extremity and requires procedural intervention in nearly half of cases. Postoperative hand therapy is inconsistently utilized, and functional benefits have not been well-characterized. To investigate whether consistent therapy attendance improves postoperative functional outcomes and quantify the impact of socioeconomic factors on recovery. Retrospective chart review. Patients at a single academic institution from 2014 to 2024 with cubital tunnel syndrome treated with surgical release were reviewed. Patient demographics, postoperative clinic visits, hand therapy attendance, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System, and Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand scores were tallied. Bivariate analysis compared patients attending four or more hand therapy sessions to those who did not. The area of deprivation was used to divide patients into two halves for analysis. A total of 1396 patients were eligible for inclusion, with 461 (33.0%) attending hand therapy for 1 [1, 4] session. Among patients attending hand therapy, patients with consistent attendance had better Pain Interference, Upper Extremity Function, and subjective pain at 3 months and latest visit. Socioeconomically deprived patients had lower therapy and clinic attendance, with worse Physical Function, Pain Interference, and Upper Extremity Function 3 months postoperatively. Socioeconomic characteristics and natural functional recovery drive hand therapy engagement. In patients who require therapy, consistent attendance provided functional and pain benefits, particularly after 3 months. Poor socioeconomic status was associated with lower hand therapy attendance and worse functional outcomes.

title: Police officer ordered to pay US$120 maintenance for three children
content:
Sekai Manyere
Herald reporter
The Harare Civil Court has ordered a Police officer to pay US$120 per month towards the upkeep of his three children, aged 10, eight and four, as well as 50 percent of their school fees.
The order followed an application by Ms Diana Janga, who had approached the court seeking US$300 per month in maintenance from her former husband, Titus Mashanga.
Ms Janga told the court that Mashanga was failing to provide adequately for their children. She presented a breakdown of the children’s monthly needs amounting to US$300 and told the court that she earns about US$200 per month as a vendor.
She told the court that Mr Mashanga is a police officer who earns US$320 and ZiG6 000, which he concurred with.
Ms Janga said she needed US$150 for the children’s fees. He offered to pay US$100 towards school fees and US$50 for children’s upkeep.
He told the court that he is also taking care of his mother, who stays in the rural areas. After hearing from both parties, Magistrate Ms Makonye Janemary ordered Mr Mashanga to pay US$120 per month and half of the children’s school fees.

title: 35 Years of Change: 10.7 Million Residents, New Cities and Tajikistan’s Green Course
content:
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan has changed noticeably: the population and cities have grown, the education and healthcare systems have expanded, the labor market has transformed, and issues of environmental protection and water resources have reached the international level.
Demographics
Over 35 years of independence, Tajikistan’s population has grown significantly, and the country has maintained its status as one of the states with a young demographic structure.
Since the early 1990s, the country’s population has more than doubled. According to the Agency on Statistics under the President of Tajikistan, as of January 1, 2026, the country was home to 10.721 million people. Population growth was driven by natural increase — high birth rates and increased life expectancy.
Today, young people make up a significant portion of the population. About a third of the country’s residents are children and teenagers, and the majority of the population is of working age. This demographic structure creates both opportunities for economic and labor market development, as well as new challenges in the areas of education, employment, and social infrastructure.
Life expectancy indicators have also changed over the years of independence. Improvements in the healthcare system, development of the social sector, and better living conditions have contributed to its growth compared to the early 1990s.
Demographic growth remains one of the key factors in Tajikistan’s development: the increase in the number of residents affects the demand for new jobs, housing construction, and the development of schools, medical facilities, and urban infrastructure.
Urbanization
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan’s cities have changed noticeably: the number of urban residents has grown, urban infrastructure has expanded, housing construction volumes have increased, and new social facilities have appeared.
From 1991 to 2026, the number of urban residents in Tajikistan increased from 1.7 million to 2.8 million people. At the same time, the share of the urban population in the country’s total population changed from 39.1% to 26.6%.
Despite the decline in share, which is associated with faster population growth in rural areas, the country’s cities took in approximately 1.1 million new residents during this period.
The capital became the prime example of urban transformation. While approximately 600,000 people lived in Dushanbe in 1991, by 2026 the city’s population had reached approximately 1.3 million residents.
Over the years of independence, the capital has expanded: new residential districts, modern roads, parks, sports, and cultural facilities have appeared.
Population growth was accompanied by an increase in construction volumes.
In January–June 2026, the volume of commissioned housing amounted to 802,900 square meters, which is 1.5 times more than during the same period of the previous year.
Over 35 years, new roads and interchanges, bridges and overpasses, schools, kindergartens, universities, medical facilities, parks, recreational areas, sports, and cultural facilities have appeared in the country’s cities.
The development of urban infrastructure has become one of the key areas of transformation in Tajikistan’s cities.
Education
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan’s education system has expanded significantly. The network of general education institutions has grown, the number of students and teachers has increased, and opportunities for vocational and higher education have expanded.
During this period, new schools, colleges, and universities have appeared, children’s enrollment in education has grown, and the number of young people obtaining a specialty and higher education has increased noticeably.
Special attention is paid to the development of preschool education, the training of teaching staff, and the establishment of new educational institutions.
Changes in the education system reflect the country’s population growth and the growing need for accessible and quality education for new generations.
Healthcare
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan’s healthcare system has expanded significantly: the number of medical facilities has increased, the number of doctors and mid-level medical personnel has grown, and opportunities for providing medical care to the population have expanded.
The development of the sector was accompanied by the construction and modernization of medical facilities, personnel training, and the strengthening of healthcare infrastructure.
Changes in the system reflect the growing demand of the population for medical services and the drive to improve the accessibility and quality of medical care.
Work and Employment
Over the years of independence, the labor market has undergone significant changes: the number of people employed in the economy has grown, labor resources have increased, and the structure of employment has changed.
The country’s economy gradually transitioned from a predominantly agrarian model to a more diverse structure, in which the service sector and industry play an increasingly important role.
At the same time, the directions of employment changed: the share of those working in agriculture declined, while the number of people employed in the service sector and other sectors of the economy increased.
The growth of labor resources has become one of the main factors in the country’s economic development, creating new challenges and opportunities for the labor market, including the need to create jobs and develop professional skills.
Environment
Over the years of independence, Tajikistan has expanded its nature conservation system, reduced pollutant emissions, and become a participant in international environmental initiatives.
During this period, the area of specially protected natural territories grew more than sevenfold — from 420,000 hectares in 1991 to 3.1 million hectares in 2025. Today, approximately 22% of the country’s territory is occupied by nature reserves, national parks, and other conservation zones.
One of the important areas of environmental policy has been the preservation of the country’s unique natural ecosystems — mountain landscapes, glaciers, and rare species of animals and plants.
Over the years of independence, emissions of pollutants from stationary sources have also decreased significantly. While their volume was 656,800 tons in 1991, in 2024 it was 129,900 tons, which is almost five times less.
Tajikistan is actively promoting the environmental agenda at the international level. On the initiative of the country, the UN declared the International Decade “Water for Life” (2005–2015), the Decade of Action “Water for Sustainable Development” (2018–2028), and 2025 as the International Year of Glacier Preservation.
Today, environmental challenges remain among the country’s top priorities: climate change, glacier retreat, water resource conservation, and biodiversity protection require ongoing efforts.

title: समाज बदल्दै पूर्वकमलरी
content:
समाज
बाल्यकाल अरूको घरमा कमलरी बसेर बिताएका कैलालीका महिलाहरू अहिले सामाजिक अभियानको नेतृत्व गरिरहेका छन्।
कैलाली। गौरीगंगा नगरपालिका-११ ऐठा गाउँकी राधिका देवी चौधरीले बाल्यकाल निकै कठिन अवस्थामा बिताइन्। मालिकको घरमा कमलरी बसेकै कारण उनले स्कुलको पाइला टेक्नसमेत पाइनन्। सानैदेखि घरायसी काममै उनको दिनचर्या बित्यो।
कमलरी जीवनपछि पनि उनको संघर्ष रोकिएन। पारिवारिक आर्थिक समस्याबीच सानै उमेरमा कमैया परिवारमा विवाह भयो। २ साउन २०५७ मा सरकारले कमैया प्रथामा बन्देज लगाउँदै कमैया मुक्तिको घोषणा गरेपछि उनका श्रीमान् रोजगारीका लागि भारत जान थाले। राधिका भने गाउँमै प्रौढ कक्षा पढ्न थालिन्।
प्रौढ कक्षाले उनको आत्मबल बढायो। १२ पुस २०६५ मा उनी मौसमी तथा बेमौसमी तरकारी खेतीसम्बन्धी तालिममा सहभागी भइन्। त्यसपछि उनले तरकारी खेती सुरु गरिन्।
तर सुरुमा श्रीमान्बाट सहयोग नपाएको उनी सुनाउँछिन्। तरकारी खेती गरेर समय बर्बाद गरेको भन्दै गालीसमेत सहनुपरेको उनको अनुभव छ। चुरा-पोते किन्नसमेत श्रीमान्सँग पैसा माग्नुपर्दा निकै गाह्रो हुने र एक-एक रुपैयाँको हिसाब दिनुपर्ने अवस्था रहेको उनी सम्झन्छिन्। त्यसबाट आफू हेपिएको महसुस भएपछि आफ्नै कमाइ हुनुपर्छ भन्ने सोचले तरकारी खेतीमा सक्रिय भएको उनी बताउँछिन्। आर्थिक रूपमा आत्मनिर्भर बन्दै गएपछि आफूलाई सन्तुष्टि मिलेको उनको अनुभव छ।
१८ कात्तिक २०७० मा उनले सुगन्ध कृषि महिला समूह गठन गरी संस्था दर्ता गरिन्। समूहको अध्यक्ष भएर सरकारी अनुदानका लागि पहल गरेको उनी सुनाउँछिन्। उनका अनुसार २०७० सालमै गाविसमार्फत आएको ‘रिजम परियोजना’अन्तर्गत समूहले कृषिका लागि ४ लाख ८० हजार ८२० रुपैयाँ अनुदान पाएको थियो।
त्यसपछि उनी विभिन्न संघसंस्थामा आबद्ध भइन्। समावेशी विकास समाजसँगको आबद्धताले आफूलाई थप बलियो र आत्मविश्वासी बनाएको उनी बताउँछिन्। उक्त संस्थाबाट आफ्नो काम आफैँ गरेर आत्मनिर्भर भएर बाँच्न सिकेको उनको अनुभव छ। अहिले ढुक्कसँग बोल्न सक्ने र आर्थिक रूपमा सक्षम भएकाले अरूसँग हात फैलाउनुपर्ने अवस्था नरहेको उनी सुनाउँछिन्।
बङ्गुरपालन, तरकारी खेती, खाजा-नास्ता तथा किराना पसल सबै जोड्दा वार्षिक १५ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढीको कारोबार
उनी गाउँघर सरसफाइ कार्यक्रमको अगुवाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापनबारे समुदायलाई प्रशिक्षण दिँदै आएकी छन्। बाटोमा गाईगोरु बाँध्न नहुने अभियान चलाएपछि गाउँको सरसफाइमा सुधार आएको उनी बताउँछिन्। नदी कटान नियन्त्रणका लागि आफ्नै पहलमा वृक्षरोपणसमेत गरेको उनको भनाइ छ।
अहिले उनी सामुदायिक मेलमिलापकर्ता र पञ्चवटी सामुदायिक वनको लेखा समिति संयोजकका रूपमा पनि सक्रिय छिन्। समुदायमा उनको छुट्टै पहिचान बनेको छ। बङ्गुरपालन, तरकारी खेती, खाजा-नास्ता तथा किराना पसल सबै जोड्दा वार्षिक १५ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढीको कारोबार हुने गरेको उनी बताउँछिन्। कारोबार बढ्दै गएपछि उनका श्रीमान् पनि भारत जान छाडेर अहिले आफ्नै बारी र व्यवसायमा सघाइरहेका छन्।
सहकारीदेखि टोल नेतृत्वसम्म
भजनी नगरपालिका-४ धनौराकी सभापति चौधरी पनि सानै उमेरमा कमलरी बस्नुपर्यो। परिवारको आर्थिक अवस्था निकै कमजोर थियो। खानलाउनकै समस्या भएपछि आफू कमलरी बस्न बाध्य भएको उनी सुनाउँछिन्।
बाल्यकालमा उनले विद्यालय जान पाइनन्। सानैमा विवाह गरेकी उनले विवाहपछि लुथरन संस्थाले सञ्चालन गरेको नौमहिने ‘ससिका’ कक्षा पढिन्। प्रौढ शिक्षाजस्तै उक्त कक्षामा दैनिक एक घण्टा पढाइ हुन्थ्यो।
त्यसपछि त्यही संस्थाले सञ्चालन गरेको तीनमहिने प्रजनन स्वास्थ्य शिक्षा र अर्को तीनमहिने कानुन तथा न्याय शिक्षा पनि उनले लिइन्। विभिन्न चरणका गरी १५ महिनाको पढाइले आफू पनि केही गर्न सक्छु भन्ने हौसला दिएको उनी बताउँछिन्।
अन्ततः २०६९ सालमा उनकै अध्यक्षतामा गरिब उत्थान ऋण तथा बचत सहकारी संस्था दर्ता भयो।
३० जनाबाट सुरु भएको उक्त सहकारीमा अहिले ४६१ सेयर सदस्य छन्। सुरुमा सदस्यले मासिक पाँच रुपैयाँ बचत गर्थे। सदस्य र कारोबारको दायरा बढ्दै जाँदा सहकारीको कुल सम्पत्ति अहिले २ करोड रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी पुगेको सभापति चौधरी बताउँछिन्।
संघसंस्थामा आबद्ध हुँदै गएपछि उनको सामुदायिक सक्रियता पनि बढ्यो। २०८१ सालमा समावेशी विकास समाजले समूह गठन गरेपछि उनी बाँसवारी टोल विकास संस्थाको अध्यक्ष भइन्। प्रत्येक महिनाको ५ गते बैठक बसेर सबैको सहभागितामा टोलका समस्यामा आधारित योजना बनाउने गरेको उनी बताउँछिन्।
उनका अनुसार आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ मा वडाबाट ३ लाख रुपैयाँ बजेट ल्याएर र स्थानीयको श्रमदानसमेत जुटाई बर्थिङ सेन्टरमा दुई वटा सेप्टिक ट्यांकी, अग्लो ठाउँमा एउटा चापाकल र ग्राउन्ड पटानीको काम गरिएको छ।
२०८२ सालमा प्रगतिशील सामुदायिक वनले प्रस्ताव स्वीकृत गरी ७५ प्रतिशत अनुदानमा गाउँका सबै ११४ घरधुरीलाई विद्युतीय चुलो वितरण गरेको थियो।
जुवातास नियन्त्रणका लागि पनि टोलका बासिन्दालाई भेला गराएर गाउँ अनुगमन र आन्तरिक सामाजिक नियम बनाइएको छ। घरमा जुवातास खेल्न नदिने, खेलेमा सुरुमा सम्झाउने र नमाने प्रहरीलाई जानकारी गराउने गरी समुदायमा सहमति गरिएको उनको भनाइ छ।
उनकै नेतृत्वमा गाउँलाई धुवाँमुक्त बनाउने उद्देश्यले भान्छाको धुवाँमुक्त अभियान पनि सञ्चालन भयो। समुदायको मागअनुसार विद्युतीय चुलोका लागि वडा कार्यालय र प्रगतिशील सामुदायिक वनमा प्रस्ताव पेस गरेको उनी बताउँछिन्।
उनका अनुसार २०८२ सालमा प्रगतिशील सामुदायिक वनले प्रस्ताव स्वीकृत गरी ७५ प्रतिशत अनुदानमा गाउँका सबै ११४ घरधुरीलाई विद्युतीय चुलो वितरण गरेको थियो।
सभापतिको परिचय सामाजिक अभियन्तामा मात्रै सीमित छैन। उनी थारू लेहङ्गा सिलाइमा पनि संलग्न छिन्। १५ वर्षसम्म लगातार थारू लेहङ्गा सिलेर राम्रो आम्दानी गरेको उनी सुनाउँछिन्। सिलाइ-कटाइबाट भएको कमाइले पक्की घर निर्माणमा समेत सहयोग पुगेको उनको भनाइ छ।गाउँघरमा केही समस्या आइपर्दा स्थानीय बासिन्दा आफूलाई खोज्दै आउने गरेको उनी बताउँछिन्।
पढ्नकै लागि कमलरी
भजनी नगरपालिका-५ लौबस्ताकी विष्णा चौधरीको कमलरी जीवन भने पढाइसँग जोडिएको छ।
घरको आर्थिक अवस्था निकै कमजोर भएपछि उनका बुवाले लम्कीका एक जग्गाधनीको डेढ बिघा जमिन अधियामा लिए। विष्णाका अनुसार जग्गा अधियामा दिएबापत उनलाई कमलरीका रूपमा घरमा पठाउने प्रस्ताव गरिएको थियो। उनका बुवाले छोरीलाई पढाइदिने सर्त राखेपछि उनी ११ वर्षको उमेरमा उक्त घरमा कमलरी बस्न गइन्।
उनी एकैपटक कक्षा तीनमा भर्ना भइन्। साँझ-बिहान घरायसी काम गर्ने र दिनभर सरकारी विद्यालयमा पढ्ने उनको दैनिकी थियो। आफूलाई कक्षा नौसम्म पढाइएको उनी बताउँछिन्। ६ वर्ष कमलरी बसेपछि गैरसरकारी संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधि उनको औपचारिक उद्धारका लागि उक्त घरमा पुगे। त्यसपछि विष्णा आफ्नै घर फर्किन् र कक्षा १० को परीक्षा दिइन्। उनले २०६८ सालमा दोस्रो श्रेणीमा एसएलसी उत्तीर्ण गरिन्।
उनलाई प्लस टु पढ्ने ठूलो इच्छा थियो। तर परिवारको आर्थिक अवस्था कमजोर भएकाले बुवाले थप पढाउन नसक्ने बताए। त्यसपछि उनी टीकापुरस्थित राज होटेलमा तीन वर्ष जागिर गर्दै प्लस टु उत्तीर्ण भइन्।
उनको पढाइ राम्रो थियो र थप पढ्ने चाहना पनि घटेन। छात्रवृत्तिका लागि उनले पटकपटक विभिन्न संघसंस्थासँग सहयोग मागिन्। अपेक्षित सहयोग नपाएपछि मुक्त कमलरी विकास मञ्चमा आबद्ध भइन्। संस्थाका पदाधिकारीबाट नेतृत्वमा आएर छात्रवृत्तिका विषयमा थप पहल गर्न सकिने सुझाव पाएपछि उनी मञ्चको गतिविधिमा सक्रिय बनेकी थिइन्।
स्नातक पढ्दै गर्दा २०७२ सालमा संस्थाका जिल्ला अध्यक्षले केही कारणवश राजीनामा दिए। रिक्त पदपूर्तिका लागि साधारणसभाले विष्णालाई जिल्ला अध्यक्ष चयन गर्यो। एक वर्षपछि उनी जिल्ला अधिवेशनबाट अध्यक्ष चुनिइन् र तीन वर्षे कार्यकाल पूरा गरिन्।
उनी अध्यक्ष भएका बेला मुक्त कमलरी विकास मञ्चले छात्रवृत्ति र आवासीय सुविधाका लागि संघीय सरकारसँग पहल गरेको उनी बताउँछिन्। उनका अनुसार मञ्चले गृह मन्त्रालयमा ज्ञापनपत्र बुझाएपछि शिक्षा मन्त्रालयमार्फत बजेट उपलब्ध भएको थियो।
उक्त पहलबाट आफूलगायत करिब २ हजार २०० मुक्त कमलरीले छात्रवृत्ति पाएको उनी बताउँछिन्। त्यस्तै होस्टेलमा खाना र बसोबासका लागि १४६ जना मुक्त कमलरीलाई उपलब्ध गराइँदै आएको मासिक ३ हजार ५०० रुपैयाँ अपुग भएको भन्दै मञ्चले रकम वृद्धिका लागि पहल गरेको थियो। त्यसपछि उक्त रकम मासिक ४ हजार ५०० रुपैयाँ पुर्याइएको विष्णाको भनाइ छ।
गाउँका धेरै जमिनदार सहरतर्फ बसाइँ सर्न थाले भने गाउँमा कमैया तथा कमलरीले पनि मुक्तिको आवाज उठाइरहेका थिए।
२०७६ सालमा उनको विवाह भयो। त्यसपछि करिब तीन वर्ष उनी गृहिणीका रूपमा घरमै केन्द्रित भइन्। सामाजिक क्षेत्रबाट टाढा हुँदा आफ्नो पहिचान गुमाउँदै गएको महसुस हुन थालेपछि पुनः पहिलेजस्तै सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा सक्रिय हुने इच्छा श्रीमान्सँग राखेको उनी सुनाउँछिन्।
श्रीमान्को सहमतिपछि २०७९ सालमा स्थानीय सरकारले कक्षा एकदेखि तीनसम्मका विद्यार्थीका लागि सञ्चालन गरेको पढाइ शिविरमा उनी स्वयंसेवकका रूपमा जोडिइन्। त्यहाँ उनले करिब तीन वर्ष काम गरिन्।
त्यही क्रममा सहकर्मी समाजले नगरपालिकामार्फत १२ दिने तालिमका लागि सूचना आह्वान गर्यो। उनले आवेदन दिइन् र छनोटमा परिन्। तालिममा राम्रो सहभागिता जनाएपछि संस्थाले उनलाई ८ कात्तिक २०८१ देखि भजनी नगरपालिका-५ मा सामाजिक परिचालकका रूपमा छनोट गर्यो।
अहिले उनी जलवायु अनुकूलन, स्थानीय सुशासन सुधार, नेतृत्व क्षमता विकास, स्थानीय सरकार र नागरिकबीचको सम्बन्ध सुधार तथा सुन्दर समाज निर्माणका लागि आवश्यक सीपबारे नागरिकलाई प्रशिक्षण दिँदै आएकी छन्।
कमलरी मुक्ति आन्दोलन र मुक्तिको घोषणा
२०५२ साल फागुनमा तत्कालीन नेपाल कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी (माओवादी)ले सशस्त्र सङ्घर्ष सुरु गरेपछि मुलुकको राजनीतिक र सामाजिक परिवेश बदलिँदै गयो। त्यसैताका गाउँका धेरै जमिनदार सहरतर्फ बसाइँ सर्न थाले भने गाउँमा कमैया तथा कमलरीले पनि मुक्तिको आवाज उठाइरहेका थिए।
अन्ततः २ साउन २०५७ मा सरकारले कमैया प्रथामा बन्देज लगायो र कमैया मुक्तिको घोषणा गर्यो।
२०५८ सालमा ‘कमैया श्रम (निषेध गर्ने) सम्बन्धी ऐन, २०५८’ जारी भयो। उक्त ऐनले कमलरीलाई पनि कमैया श्रमिकको परिभाषाभित्र समेटेको थियो। कमैया मुक्तिको घोषणा र कानुनी व्यवस्था आएपछि कमलरी पनि मुक्त भएको अपेक्षा गरिएको थियो।
दाङको गोबरडिहास्थित खैरा गाउँबाट २०५६ सालमा सुरु भएको कमलरी मुक्ति आन्दोलनले अन्ततः २०७० सालमा औपचारिक सफलता पायो।
तर कानुनी व्यवस्था हुँदैमा व्यवहारमा कमलरी प्रथा तत्काल अन्त्य भएन। मुक्त भनिएका धेरै कमैया परिवारको उचित पुनःस्थापना हुन नसक्दा उनीहरूका छोरी फेरि कमलरी बस्न बाध्य भएका घटना दोहोरिइरहे।
समयक्रममा कमलरीहरू क्रमशः सचेत र संगठित हुँदै गए। उनीहरूले आफूहरू परिवारदेखि राज्यसम्मका लैङ्गिक विभेदकारी मूल्य, नीति र व्यवहारका कारण शिक्षा र अवसरबाट वञ्चित भई दासमय जीवनमा फसाइएको महसुस गर्न थाले। त्यसपछि कमलरीहरूले आफ्नै मुक्तिका लागि अभियान सुरु गरे। मालिकका घरबाट बाहिर निस्किएर उनीहरू आन्दोलनमा उत्रिए।
कमलरी उन्मूलन अभियान चल्यो, तर मुक्तिका लागि उनीहरूले लामो सङ्घर्ष गर्नुपर्यो। यस क्रममा कमलरीहरू पटकपटक राजधानी काठमाडौँ धाए। कहिले मुक्ति, कहिले पुनःस्थापना, कहिले छात्रवृत्ति त कहिले शोषणमा परेकाहरूको उद्धारको माग गर्दै २०६५ सालदेखि नै उनीहरूले काठमाडौँमा धर्ना र प्रदर्शन गरे। ‘कमलरी प्रथा उन्मूलन गरौँ, बालिका बचाऔँ’ भन्ने नारासहित काठमाडौँमा भएका आन्दोलनका क्रममा प्रहरीसँग झडप र बल प्रयोगका घटना पनि भए। दाङको गोबरडिहास्थित खैरा गाउँबाट २०५६ सालमा सुरु भएको कमलरी मुक्ति आन्दोलनले अन्ततः २०७० सालमा औपचारिक सफलता पायो।
२४ जेठ २०७० मा कमलरी प्रथा उन्मूलनका लागि संयुक्त सङ्घर्ष समिति र सरकारबीच १० बुँदे सहमति भयो। सहमतिमा तत्कालीन महिला, बालबालिका तथा समाज कल्याणमन्त्री ऋद्धिबाबा प्रधान र कमलरी प्रथा उन्मूलनका लागि संयुक्त सङ्घर्ष समितिका संयोजक तथा थारू कल्याणकारिणी सभाका केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष चन्द्रकुमार चौधरी थारूले हस्ताक्षर गरेका थिए।
सरकारी र मञ्चको तथ्याङ्कबीच अन्तर रहे पनि राधिका, सभापति र विष्णाजस्ता पूर्व कमलरीको जीवनमा आएको परिवर्तनले मुक्तिपछिको अर्को पाटो देखाउँछ।
नेपालमा कमैया मुक्तिपछि पनि कमलरीलाई छुट्टै रूपमा मुक्त हुन थप १३ वर्ष लाग्यो। १३ असार २०७० को मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले कमलरी मुक्तिको घोषणा गर्ने र अभियानकै रूपमा आवश्यक कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने निर्णय गर्यो। कमलरी श्रमिक राखेबापत कसैले कुनै किसिमको रकम लेनदेन गरेको भए त्यस्तो रकम निष्क्रिय हुने र कमलरी वा उनको परिवारले उक्त रकम फिर्ता गर्नु नपर्ने व्यवस्था पनि निर्णयमा समेटिएको थियो।
त्यसबेलाको सरकारी लगतमा कुल मुक्त कमलरीको सङ्ख्या नौ हजार ४९० थियो। मुक्त कमलरी विकास मञ्चले सङ्कलन गरेको आँकडामा भने मुक्त कमलरीको सङ्ख्या १२ हजार ७६९ थियो।
सरकारी र मञ्चको तथ्याङ्कबीच अन्तर रहे पनि राधिका, सभापति र विष्णाजस्ता पूर्व कमलरीको जीवनमा आएको परिवर्तनले मुक्तिपछिको अर्को पाटो देखाउँछ। बाल्यकाल अरूको घरमा श्रम गर्दै बिताएका उनीहरू अहिले आफ्नै आयआर्जन, सामाजिक नेतृत्व र समुदायका समस्यामा हस्तक्षेप गर्ने भूमिकामा पुगेका छन्।

title: I couldn't cook when I left home – but these easy £2.50 recipes became my go-to
content:
I couldn't cook when I left home – but these easy £2.50 recipes became my go-to
- Published
When Mia Jones left her home in Anglesey to go to university in London, she couldn't cook "whatsoever" - but quickly realised this had to change.
"I couldn't live off pasta for the rest of my life," she says - and all the ready meals and pot noodles were starting to add up.
"I'd be spending £45 a week on food," says the 22-year-old. "That wasn't viable."
So she started buying fresh ingredients. "Then I realised, 'Oh, I need to learn how to cook now.'" She started following social media videos for tips and recipes, swapping out foods she didn't like.
While there were some early disasters it was not long before Mia was proud to say she could cook.
"It made me realise I could function on my own and live on my own", she says. "[First year] me would not be able to believe it all".
What's more, Mia cut her weekly shop by £20 - and found she had more energy.
"I was feeling a lot more awake in my lectures, which was very useful," she says.
After finishing her masters degree she now shares her recipes online, hoping to help other students in the same position she was in.
The Food Chain
Rumella Dasgupta asks what dishes you should be able to cook when you leave home for the first time
Mia and other once culinary-challenged students have shared the signature dishes they learned that were cheap, easy - and most importantly tasty.
All of the recipes can be made by stocking up a starter store cupboard for under £13. Then each meal uses additional ingredients for under £2.50 - which make several portions perfect for the next day or popping in the freezer.
We asked retail tracking platform Assosia to find the rough cost of standard sized packs of ingredients using the average pre-promotion price across Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda & Morrisons on 11 September 2026.
Mia's go-to dishes: chickpea curry and udon noodles with tofu
Mia's first recipe is a chickpea curry: "It's very cheap and very nutritious," she says. Click here to watch her make the dish.
The second is udon noodles. "It's a 10 minute recipe, it's easily customisable [with tofu or chicken] and really useful for a weeknight dinner." Mia says she'll add chilli oil if she's feeling fancy. Click here , externalto watch her make the dish.
Like Mia, Jayda Otuo-Mensah "didn't really cook" before going to university.
The physiotherapy student wanted to know how to make healthy food while spending around 40 hours a week on placement in hospitals.
"It's a lot easier when you're cooking because you know exactly what's going in," she says.
"I can have a chicken burger and it's really healthy because of the way I cooked it."
After "a lot of trial and error" following TikTok videos, the 20-year-old Coventry University student felt confident enough to film herself cooking.
Now she buys staples, and while she tries to stick to a weekly meal plan she mostly cooks what she is feeling.
Jayda's go-to dish: crispy teriyaki mince tacos
One of the meals Jayda makes the most is tacos.
"It's a great meal to learn; it's quick and affordable," she says. Click here , externalto watch her make the dish.
Rob Medhurst credits the student staple of spaghetti bolognese as being his springboard onto greater dishes.
"It's very affordable and it's easy," says the 25-year-old graduate of Nottingham Trent University.
"I quickly learned meal prepping and batch cooking was the best way for me," he says.
"I know some people love the art of cooking but personally I don't."
Rob's go-to dish: spaghetti bolognese
Rob has found the simple spag bol a versatile recipe: "You can just adapt a couple of things for chilli or lots of burritos."
He says he's made the same recipe so many times he describes it as "muscle memory".
Remember to bring the store cupboard essentials
Chef and cookbook author Claire Thompson remembers her daughter Grace leaving home to go to university, and wondering: "Can she really cook?"
She sent Grace off with three crates of supplies, which her daughter described as being "stocked for the apocalypse just in case anything went awry".
But for Claire there are certain essentials everyone should consider stocking up on when leaving home.
"I think spices are a really good thing to start getting your head around," she told the BBC World Service's The Food Chain podcast.
"They deliver lots and lots of flavour for not very much money, and they last well in your store cupboard," she says.
"Adding a jar of chickpeas to a tomato sauce and adding that [to] your pasta, you're boosting really good levels of protein and bringing nutrients to a really pretty cheap dish really."

title: Civil registration drive helps fix gaps in vital records
content: Philomene Nyirambabazi believed all her five children were properly registered after birth. But when the resident of Nyamugari Cell in Gasaka Sector, Nyamagabe District took them for photographs as part of the ongoing digital identity registration exercise, she discovered that her youngest child, an eight-year-old, had never been registered in the civil registration system. ALSO READ: Relief as Rwanda eases registration of births She was directed to the cell office, where the child was registered and given a number to proceed with digital ID registration. “I thought all my children had been registered, but it turned out that some were not. The civil registration services they brought closer to us have been very helpful,” Nyirambabazi said. She is among citizens who have used the ongoing civil registration exercise to register children, correct errors in their records and access other services. The exercise was held as Rwanda marked African Civil Registration Day and officially launched Civil Registration Week under the theme “Proper civil registration, the foundation of quality services.” The week is intended to help citizens who have not accessed civil registration services, including those who have not registered their children, while also allowing people to correct errors in their existing records. ALSO READ: Civil registration is an obligation and right of every Rwandan – Mukabaramba The activity also included photographing citizens for the Single Digital ID, with local authorities assisting residents to resolve issues identified in their civil registration records. Minister of Local Government Dominique Habimana, who was in Nyamagabe to officially launch civil registration week, said accurate civil registration is essential for both citizens and national development. “For us to achieve the development we aspire to, the country needs to have a clear record of its population and accurate demographic statistics,” Habimana said. He said such information enables government to properly plan for infrastructure and public services, including schools, health facilities, water and electricity, as well as settlement planning. Rwanda has also digitised several civil registration services to make them easier and faster to access. Citizens can obtain documents through Irembo platform without having to travel long distances or spend a full day at government offices. Birth and death registration services are provided at health facilities and cell offices free of charge, while an electronic system known as e-Death Notification allows village leaders to report deaths electronically. ALSO READ: Citizens urged on timely registration of death, birth events Habimana encouraged citizens and local leaders to make use of the system. Other civil registration services, including marriage registration, child recognition and establishing parentage, are provided at sector level and at Rwandan embassies abroad. The minister also encouraged couples living together without being legally married to approach local authorities and formalise their union, saying this has benefits for the couples, their children and the family as a whole. The ongoing exercise has also enabled residents to identify errors in information already contained in the civil registration system. Rafael Munyaneza, a resident of Kabacuzi Village in Nyamagabe Cell, brought two of his children to be photographed for the digital ID when he discovered errors in their records. One child had been recorded as having been born in Gitega Sector, Nyarugenge District, while the other had an incorrect date of birth. The errors were corrected within minutes before the children were photographed. ALSO READ: Digitisation takes centre stage as Rwanda launches civil registration week Munyaneza said he understood that having accurate personal information in the system makes it easier to access key services, including those related to marriage and property transactions. “When your civil registration records are in order, it speeds up every service you need related to civil registration,” he said. The activities were held in Nyamagabe, which was recognised as the best-performing district nationally in civil registration services during the 2025/26 financial year. The district scored 95.4 percent, followed by Nyarugenge with 95.3 percent, Gicumbi at 94.7 percent, Gakenke at 94.6 percent and Ruhango at 93.8 percent. The ranking was based on districts’ average performance in birth registration, death registration and verbal autopsy between July 2025 and July 2026. Minister Habimana presented Nyamagabe Mayor Hildebrand Niyomwungeri with an award recognising the district’s performance. Niyomwungeri attributed the result to awareness campaigns and efforts by residents and local officials to improve access to civil registration services. He, however, said limited access to digital technology and internet connectivity sometimes delay services, while some cases require citizens to go through the justice system. He said the district would continue working to address the challenges and improve service delivery.
